---
title: "Story: The Impact of Daily Activity"
subtitle: "How exercise and movement shape a Golden Retriever's lifespan"
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

```{r}
#| label: story-plot
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

library(tidyverse)

dogs <- read_csv("golden_retrievers.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |> 
  mutate(activity_level = factor(activity_level, levels = c("Low", "Moderate", "High")))

dogs |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = activity_level, y = lifespan_years, fill = activity_level)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "The Power of Play: Daily Exercise and Longevity",
    subtitle = "Dogs with high daily activity live nearly a full year longer than sedentary dogs",
    x = "Activity Level",
    y = "Life Expectancy (years)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Blues")
```

When looking at factors influencing a Golden Retriever's health, diet and weight often get the most attention. However, our dataset of 10,000 dogs reveals another critical factor: daily physical activity.

Golden Retrievers with high activity levels live to an average of **12.2 years**, compared to **11.3 years** for dogs with low activity levels. Regular walks, fetching, and active playtime provide cardiovascular benefits and joint mobility that appear to add nearly an entire extra year of companionship.
